newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary may cut devalution in H2 1997 - government.
newsitem.headline: Hungary may cut devalution in H2 1997 - government.

text.p: Hungary said on Thursday it expects to continue its monthly 1.2 percent devaluations at least till mid-1997 but might then reduce them.
"No opportunity seems to offer itself for the reduction of the devaluation rate," said a government decision released by spokesman Elemer Kiss.

But the projected decline of inflation, the amount of the current account deficit and the inflow of foreign capital may enable the country to cut the devaluation rate in the second half of 1997, the text added.
Hungary aims to cut inflation to 18 percent in 1997 from a forecast of 22 to 24 percent for this year, and to reduce the current account deficit to $1.5 billion from the $2 billion targeted for 1996.
